page.layout: One page of running text in one column. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Centred heading "VERSVS III." with an italic verse line below it, then two paragraphs. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: quæ fit cùm exorbitat homo à Dei semitis: hoc est, cùm à vero, sanctoq; aberrat: & effusio gressuum, quæ fit cùm in lubrico temere oberrans, aquæ in morem corruens quodámodo effunditur: id, in quam, Apostolo nostro est, σαλεύεσθαι ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν [?], hoc est, nimium commoueri & perturbari oppresionibus, quæ veritatis profesionem comitari solent, 1. Thess. 3.3. & σαλευθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ νοὸς [?], id est, à mete dimoueri & turbari. Persuasum enim habuerat Asaph, secū dum internum hominem, veros Israelitas Deo cordi caros q; esse: sed carne tumultuã te & contradicente, nonnihil obscuratam sensit veram illam sententiam & fiduciam sui cordis.
Quare me quoq; ad Dei gloriã, & meam correptionem & institutionem, fateri erro rem meum æquum sanè fuerit: & multis a lijs idem experientibus utilissimum.
main_text.head: VERSUS III.

p.i: Quia exastuaui propter superbos, pacem (id est, prosperitatem) impiorum cernens.

main_text.p: Quæ autem erroris illius causa fuit? Sophisma carnis, cuius hæc sententia est.
Profectò causa magna est, cur quis suspi-cetur

page.notes: Scan is slightly blurred and the Greek is faint. The Greek at "Apostolo nostro est" (1 Thess. 3:3, σαλεύεσθαι ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν) and the Greek after "1. Thess. 3.3. &" (σαλευθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ νοὸς) are my best reading and are marked [?]. The verse first word "exastuaui" is uncertain (possibly exaestuaui) and is not marked here, so check it against the original. "à mete" appears as printed (possibly mente). "secū dum" is a line-end split with the n abbreviated by a tilde over u. "alijs" is printed with j.
